title: NYC Building Monitor
generalDescription: An app that uses NYC open property data, census data, and NYU Furman Center CoreData to visualize income, rent, and city service distributions throughout the city, by census tract & neighborhood, on a map. This app uses Python to clean & process the data as well as GIS libraries to create database associations where foreign keys are missing but coordinates exist. This project would lead me to my work on DAP Portal with ANHD, a tool built for NYC Council & housing advocacy groups.

title: Ephemeris.js
generalDescription: An Ephemeris (or \"sky journal\") is a tool which gives you the trajectories and celestial coordinates of a astronomical body like the moon, planets, comets, etc, at any given point in time. This can be used for astronomical endeavors and also, in my case, astrology projects. Modern epherides use formula to project these coordinates thousands of years into the future, though often the level of computing power and precision needed means they usually are computed & saved to a database table for later access. Not so surprisingly, many Ephemeris implementations are beyond paywalls (such as the Swiss Ephemeris). Most of the code on Github is a wrapper for the Swiss Ephmeris API, which I simply won't tolerate for any of my projects when this code can be free. Fortunately I found a Javascript implementation of Moshier's Ephemeris on Github. Moshier's ephemeris provides formula for obtaining the positions of the sun, moon, planets, and asteroids at any moment from 3000 B.C.E. to 3000 C.E. It was just a matter of forking the repo and updating it to use ES6 and class instances for implementation. Then, I went a few steps further and added my own support for calculating retrograde motion in all the bodies and calculating the lunar nodes. As far as I know, this is the only Javascript Ephemeris out there which does any of these things.
technicalDescription: Javascript, ES6, maintained open source project

title: Circular Natal Horoscope JS
generalDescription: Building off my ephemeris work I created a Javascript library specifically suited for creating circular natal horoscope charts. To create a complete chart, you need to calculate dozens of different things. A charts needs to: 1. Evaluate someone's birth date, time, and coordinates (lat/lng) 2. Calculate: - the apparent positions & motion of all the celestial bodies in that moment (the ephmeris does this part) - the cusps of each house using 1 of a dozen house systems - (this project provides 5) - calculate the angles & aspects beween each significant point on the chart (using geometry) - provide a set of coordinates for plotting all of these cusps and points to the chart's frontend code 3. Provide quality of life features - a language translation system for labels (for international users) - configurable orbs for the aspects (since astrologers are known to debate the appropriate size of these) And this library does all of these things except for rendering the actual chart. I decided to **only** include calculations in this project and make it frontend-agnostic because I could see how useful a library like this would be to so many projects and hobbysts that may want to build their own frontend implementation. This is my contribution to the JS astrology community and it's quite popular on github where I maintain the project & collaborate with others to improve its features. As far as I know, this is the only ES6 Javascript chart calculation project on Github that doesn't rely on an external API.
technicalDescription: ES6, Javascript, maintained open source project

title: Astrology Tech Jewelry
generalDescription: With the help of **Astronomical Algorithims** by Jean Meeus, I've transposed a number of astronomical formulas into C++ code which can run on an Arduino. My first project is the Moonstone, an Arduino connected to a real-time clock and a TFT screen. The micro-controller calculates the moon's current phase & illumination fraction as well as its apparent longitude along the ecliptic. This allows me to render an up-to-the-minute projection of the moon's current appearance and display the zodiac sign it's inhabiting in this moment. In the future, I plan on 3D printing an enclosure for the screen & components and making my own jewelry.
technicalDescription: C++, electronics, Arduino Microcontroller (itsy-bitsy m0), RS3231 RTC, TFT Screen, jewelry (found)
